releaseGate.reason: Current per-drive loopback ports share one cookie host. Fixture evidence and hand-authored capture JSON cannot establish browser provenance, so the current release checker must remain blocked.
requires: A reviewed, scalable per-drive cookie-isolating host design with distinct cookie hosts.
A real Electron WebContents capture JSON showing both app URLs, WebContents IDs, origins, localStorage, cookies, and IndexedDB in one browser profile, with its matching SHA-256 digest.
A trusted Electron runtime capture/review integration must bind measured WebContents output to the tested build and profile; a human reviewer must confirm its provenance.
After that integration is implemented and independently reviewed, a passing origin-isolation evidence check must include cookie-host, storage, strict-CSP, lifecycle, and bridge proof.

commands.evidence: Runtime smoke JSON shows backend readiness, proxy port, and relay status.
Peerit navigates through the production RPC/proxy path without approving a third-party trust prompt.
Diagnostic-only HyperProxy/HttpBridge fixture. Its evidence artifact must remain blocked by the release checker; it does not observe Chromium cookies or storage.

notes: Runs a local HyperProxy/HttpBridge harness with per-drive origins enabled.
Uses the plan apps as fixture drive identities and exercises proxy, CSP injection, listener release, and bridge routes.
Fixture storage buckets are simulated. The release checker must block this output until a separate real Electron WebContents capture and distinct cookie hosts exist.

manualSteps.action: Open Peerit (hyper://ec6e2d6d9d22b9d6b40e11a9ca3042be3197e4bdca9e9a7f079be6ee830761b4/) and Pearfeed (hyper://5c2807c5ba1383e55d69a2fe5085fdeb563e2e18f175f363f3f18437219c1aec/) in separate PearBrowser tabs while the feature flag is enabled.
manualSteps.evidence: Screenshots or console output show both tabs loaded.

manualSteps.action: In each tab, record `location.origin` from DevTools.
manualSteps.evidence: Record both exact origins and hostnames. Different ports on 127.0.0.1 do not isolate cookies; this release gate requires distinct cookie hosts.

manualSteps.action: Review the per-drive loopback host design and verify App A and App B use distinct cookie hostnames in one Electron profile. Do not substitute separate ports on 127.0.0.1.
manualSteps.evidence: Design review and Electron navigation capture show a scalable mapping from each drive key to its own cookie host, including restart and listener lifecycle behavior.

manualSteps.action: Run the write snippet in Peerit.
manualSteps.evidence: Peerit reports its origin and writes localStorage, cookie, and IndexedDB proof values.

manualSteps.action: Run the read snippet in Pearfeed.
manualSteps.evidence: Pearfeed reports a different cookie host and reads no pear-origin-isolation-proof value from localStorage, cookie, or IndexedDB in the same real Electron profile.

manualSteps.action: Capture both page results from actual Electron WebContents, along with the browser build/source commit, OS, one-profile identifier, and artifact path. Attach the unmodified capture to the release evidence.
manualSteps.evidence: Record storage.capture.kind, artifact path, and matching SHA-256, then have a human reviewer inspect WebContents IDs, runtime version, timestamp, build, and one-profile provenance. The current checker still blocks this hand-authored record until trusted runtime capture/review integration exists.

manualSteps.action: Load at least one strict-CSP real app under the feature flag.
manualSteps.evidence: The app loads its assets and Pear bridge without CSP console failures caused by per-drive origin mode.

manualSteps.action: Close Peerit, or navigate its tab to Pearfeed, then keep Pearfeed open.
manualSteps.evidence: PearBrowser stays responsive and subsequent app navigation still works, confirming the release path did not break tab-origin lifecycle behavior.

manualSteps.action: Run a real app bridge flow such as Peerit identity/sync under the feature flag.
manualSteps.evidence: `/api/identity`, `/api/sync/*`, `/api/swarm/ticket`, and `/api/swarm/events?ticket=` continue to work from the per-drive origin.

automatedVerifier.note: Diagnostic fixture scaffold only. It must not be relabeled as browser evidence; a future trusted Electron capture/review integration is required.

acceptance: Feature flag is enabled for the launched desktop process.
Two app tabs report different `location.origin` values and different cookie hostnames.
A trusted Electron runtime capture/review flow proves, from one browser profile, that App A localStorage, cookie, and IndexedDB values are not visible in App B.
Strict-CSP real app compatibility is recorded.
Tab close/navigation-away does not leave the browser in a broken listener state.
At least one real app bridge flow still passes under the feature flag.
remainingIfPassed: Review the cookie-isolating host design and listener lifecycle on supported desktop platforms.
Only after the trusted capture/review gate is implemented should the operator record a passing checker report and make a release claim.
